column3: The Hebrew commands setting him high and leaves the house’s owner unnamed in the heading; BSB says protect and names David’s house.
The Hebrew says they run and prepare, and asks God to awake to meet him; BSB explicitly describes attacking him and helping him.
The Hebrew has a singular dog; BSB has dogs.
The Hebrew names swords on their lips and does not separately express us as object of hearing; BSB says sharp words and adds us.
The Hebrew names his strength; BSB addresses my strength.
The Hebrew calls Him God of my loving devotion and says he will look on his enemies; BSB says my God of loving devotion and stare down his foes.
The Hebrew says make them wander; BSB says scatter them.
The Hebrew has a singular mouth and sin; BSB has mouths and sins.
The Hebrew has an active plural they will know; BSB uses passive it may be known.
The Hebrew has a singular dog; BSB has dogs.
The Hebrew describes passing the night when unsatisfied; BSB says growling.
The Hebrew describes God as having been his fortress; BSB says You are my fortress.
The Hebrew says God is my fortress without directly repeating You in that clause; BSB directly addresses You, O God.
